# v0.1.0 upgrade fixture

Generated by app/scripts/make-upgrade-fixture.ts using **v0.1.0**, commit
`570b8032418cbbfc01a20cc0f64257135cd6c5ef` (the annotated tag points to this commit). Fictional text and one-second
16 kHz float32 silence buffers only. No real data, credentials, models, or network AI.
The public fixture is text-only: meetings.sql contains the schema and all rows;
audio.json describes the relative paths and byte lengths of zero-filled float32
audio. No database/recording binaries or base64 audio are stored in Git.

From app/, with dependencies linked in both checkouts:

```sh
nice -n 19 env -u GEMINI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY node --experimental-strip-types scripts/make-upgrade-fixture.ts /path/to/disposable-v0.1.0 /path/to/NEW-upgrade-v0.1.0
```

The generator refuses another commit, modified tracked old code, or an existing output.
Fictional external assets are created only at the fixed neutral absolute path
/private/tmp/hearalong-upgrade-v0.1.0-assets, never under a checkout, home or scratch
folder. The generator refuses to run if that path already exists, resolves its
real path before calling the old writers, and removes the assets on completion.
The privacy test scans every fixture file as bytes, including meetings.sql and
audio.json, and rejects binary recording/database extensions.
It uses the old server's settings/AI-save APIs, MeetingStore, Projects, Memory,
NotesFile/validator, Boards/scanner, ActionJobs, Explorations, plan checker,
PlanVersions and PlanTodos. No hand-written SQL data. After the WAL checkpoint,
upgrade-fixture-sql.ts reads the old database with the same node:sqlite library
as the app (no sqlite3 CLI or new package). It emits schema in kind/name order
and rows in original rowid order, retaining rowids, user_version and application_id.
expected.json records every table's row count and SHA-256 of its SQL-quoted column
values/rowids, plus the schema. The dump is deterministic for the same database;
fresh generation still gets the old writers' new UUIDs and timestamps.

At test time only, the fixture is copied to a disposable folder, node:sqlite
rebuilds meetings.sqlite and Buffer.alloc recreates the five silent recordings.
Before starting the app, the test compares every rebuilt table and schema against
the old-writer snapshot in expected.json. It removes meetings.sql and audio.json
from that copy, then takes the file-preservation baseline of the materialized
folder. Upgrade data assertions remain HTTP-only. expected.json is the old-writer
HTTP oracle as well, not a current-code-generated snapshot.

Coverage: two meetings (one in a project), modes/intervals, repo and material paths,
project and meeting glossaries, completed/failed/cancelled/deferred-retry chunks,
retry attempts, corrected/raw text and edit spans, a sealed frame and capture
settings, latest notes at version 2, two cards including an interrupted auto
reservation, a failed answer, a published plan/run and accepted plan to-do,
three memory item types, event timelines, two brief versions, non-default
settings, local/cloud model choices and fictional-provider consent.

The reserved board is a byte-for-byte snapshot of the old writer at its durable
reserve-before-submit boundary, restored after the fake answer finishes. On open
it must become uncertain, not be automatically resubmitted.

Limits of the release: NotesFile overwrites earlier note bodies (only v2 survives);
sealed frame bytes are removed by sealWindow (its row survives and duplicate
HTTP frame admission checks its identity). Materials and repo paths are absolute
external references, not copied attachments: their original fictional files are
in fictional-assets for inspection, but their recorded paths intentionally no
longer exist once the generator removes the fixed neutral external-assets folder. The test checks that
those references are unchanged; it does not invent relocation of external files.
v0.1.0 already writes SQLite materials/glossaries and quick/main board settings;
it has no autoAnswers setting and cannot naturally produce pre-project materials.json/glossaries .migrated files
or luna/sol board choices, or missing columns it already creates. Those older
formats are not fabricated into this release fixture.
